'''Paul B. Wiegmann''' (Павел Борисович Вигман) is a Russian [[physicist]]. He is the Robert W. Reneker Distinguished Service Professor in the Department of Physics at the [[University of Chicago]], [[James Franck Institute]] and [[Enrico Fermi Institute]].<ref name="physics.uchicago">{{cite web|title=University of Chicago page about Paul Wiegmann|url=https://physics.uchicago.edu/page/paul-wiegmann|access-date=2017-03-18|archive-date=2017-03-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170318173452/https://physics.uchicago.edu/page/paul-wiegmann|url-status=dead}}</ref> He specializes in [[theoretical condensed matter physics]]. He made pioneering contributions to the field of [[Integrable system#Quantum integrable systems|quantum integrable systems]]. He found exact solutions of [[O(3) Non-linear Sigma Model]], {{harv|Wiegmann|1985}}, [[Wess–Zumino–Witten model]] (together with [[Alexander Markovich Polyakov|Alexander Polyakov]]), [[Anderson impurity model]] and multi-channel [[Kondo model]] (with [[Alexei Tsvelik]]).<ref name="sciencedirect">{{cite journal|title=Physics Letters A: The exact solution of the s-d exchange model with arbitrary impurity spin S (Kondo problem)|doi=10.1016/0375-9601(81)90056-6 | volume=81|issue=2–3|journal=Physics Letters A|pages=179–184|year=1981|last1=Fateev|first1=V.A.|last2=Wiegmann|first2=P.B.|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/125993 }}</ref>

== Notable Achievements and Scientific Recognition ==

In 2003, Paul Wiegmann was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], the official citation <ref name="aps">{{cite web|title=American Physical Society DCMP Fellows, 2003|url=http://www.aps.org/units/dcmp/fellowship/index.cfm?year=2003}}</ref> indicating that the recognition was  "For exact solutions of models of interacting electronic systems and quantum field theory, including the multi-channel Kondo problem and the Anderson model for magnetic impurities."
